problem_text:
A logistics company must coordinate a maintenance circuit for five specialized machinery units situated at distinct facilities.  
The geographical positions of these units are recorded as follows:  
Unit Alpha: coordinates (74,180)  
Unit Beta: coordinates (31,140)  
Unit Gamma: coordinates (85,138)  
Unit Delta: coordinates (52,154)  
Unit Epsilon: coordinates (140,150)  

Travel distances between units, measured in kilometers, are precisely known:  
Alpha to Gamma: 43.4 km  
Alpha to Delta: 34.1 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 72.5 km  
Beta to Gamma: 54.0 km  
Beta to Delta: 25.2 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 109.5 km  
Gamma to Delta: 36.7 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 56.3 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 88.1 km  

Due to access restrictions, no direct route exists between Unit Alpha and Unit Beta.  
Furthermore, owing to scheduling and permit limitations, exactly one of the following two connections must be incorporated into the inspection circuit: the link between Unit Beta and Unit Gamma, or the link between Unit Gamma and Unit Delta.  

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed-loop inspection route that visits each unit exactly once and returns to the starting point.
